Its work included inhaler devices and biological medicines developed and manufactured in Turkey.

long_biography.plain_text:
During his years as a co-owner of Vinero, Zafer Toksöz helped introduce visitors to its vineyards on Turkey’s Gallipoli Peninsula. Walking the estate with its technical team, he explained how the soil retained water while allowing drainage. The project brought together a winery and a hotel among the vines.

Vinero pursued Bordeaux-style wines with advice from Michel Rolland and winemaker Aslı Bayhan. Its gravity-fed cellar moved grapes and wine through tanks and pipes without pumps, combining traditional clarification with modern equipment. The hotel took its name from Seçkin Pirim’s entrance sculpture, linking the estate’s wine and hospitality under the Porta Caeli name.

confidence.reason: Firsthand estate visit records personal participation and concrete production and hospitality details. Past-tense ownership respects the subsequent disposal.
